symptoms: Shortness of breath, especially during physical activity or exertion
Cough with a lot of mucus
Constant feeling of not being able to get enough air
causes: Anything that causes long-term inflammation in your lungs
Exposure to cigar and marijuana smoke
Exposure to dust or chemical fumes from your job or hobbies
Exposure to smoke from campfires or wood-burning stoves
treatments: Inhaled corticosteroids to reduce airway inflammation
Oral corticosteroids to treat symptom flare-ups (exacerbations)
Oxygen therapy to get more oxygen to your lungs
Lung volume reduction surgery (LVRS) to remove damaged parts of your lungs
Bronchoscopic lung volume reduction to place valves in your lungs that release and prevent trapped air
life_expectancy: Depends on your lung function and the severity of symptoms at diagnosis
Depends on whether or not you smoke or used to smoke
Depends on whether you have Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency
If you have limited damage and it’s not progressing, you may have a normal life expectancy
If emphysema is in the later stages at diagnosis, it can shorten your life by six to nine years
outlook: What to expect depends on the severity of the disease when you’re diagnosed
People who are diagnosed earlier tend to have better outcomes
If you quit smoking and avoid other lung irritants, you can slow down the progression of emphysema and reduce your risk of new damage
The existing damage is permanent and can get worse over time
With treatment, many people manage their symptoms and improve their quality of life
diagnosis: Tapping on chest to listen for hollow sounds
Blood tests, including genetic testing to diagnose Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency
complications: High levels of carbon dioxide in your blood (hypercapnia)
Low levels of oxygen in your blood (hypoxemia)
High blood pressure in your lungs
Polycythemia vera, when your body makes too many red blood cells
prevention: Ask a healthcare provider for resources to help you quit if you currently smoke
Avoid dust and toxins in the air
Wear a respirator mask if you need to be around things that can irritate your lungs
Wearing a mask when you’re around others who could be sick
